tasks.title: Parse @project:task-id in DependsOn (Cross-project task dependencies)
tasks.description: DependsOn accepts @project:task-id and resolves it to the named sub-project.

tasks.title: Validate cross-project DAGs (Cross-project task dependencies)
tasks.description: Cycle detection and readiness checks span sub-projects, so a cross-project cycle is refused.

tasks.title: Readiness honours cross-project edges (Cross-project task dependencies)
tasks.description: A task blocked by another project is not reported ready, in CLI and MCP alike.

tasks.title: Define the dispatch contract (Per-task subagent dispatch)
tasks.description: A task handed to a subagent carries its spec citation, acceptance criteria, and the tool to report completion through.

tasks.title: Deterministic completion hook (Per-task subagent dispatch)
tasks.description: A dispatched task completes through a recorded transition, so the audit trail attributes the work to that agent and session.

tasks.title: Drift gate for CI (Spec-to-PR loop)
tasks.description: A documented CI job runs drift detect on merge and fails or reports based on severity.

tasks.title: Open a follow-up for unaccepted drift (Spec-to-PR loop)
tasks.description: Drift left unaccepted after merge becomes a tracked issue rather than a silent divergence.

tasks.title: Emit an explain-and-patch prompt (Drift explainer follow-ups)
tasks.description: roady drift explain can emit a request whose expected format is a patch, with the write-back tool named.

tasks.title: Declare member repositories (Cross-repo planning)
tasks.description: A workspace lists member repos and resolves their .roady/ directories.

tasks.title: Aggregate plan state across members (Cross-repo planning)
tasks.description: Status, report, and drift span every member repo in one view.

tasks.title: Generated ids are safe to use as ids (Field-reported reliability)
tasks.description: Feature and task ids must be usable as a path component, a URL segment and a shell argument. Improving the derivation must not re-identify features that already exist. (#74)

tasks.title: Documentation is written to the project it belongs to (Field-reported reliability)
tasks.description: add_feature must resolve docs/backlog.md against the project root rather than the process working directory, and must not report a sync that did not happen. (#71)

tasks.title: Plan writes resolve the feature they name (Field-reported reliability)
tasks.description: A task written back with a feature title, or a legacy id, must be linked to the right feature; a link that resolves to nothing must be reported to the caller rather than stored silently. (#73)

tasks.title: Task listings fit in the caller context (Field-reported reliability)
tasks.description: roady_tasks must page and project its results, and must say when it truncated rather than returning a partial list that looks complete. (#75)

tasks.title: MCP errors carry the actionable message (Field-reported reliability)
tasks.description: A domain error must reach the MCP client as the message the CLI gives, not as a bare internal error. (#72)

tasks.title: Tool names mirror the CLI (MCP surface is learnable, trimmable and honest)
tasks.description: MCP tools are named noun-first to match the CLI verbs (roady_spec_add, not roady_add_feature), so knowledge of one surface transfers to the other. Breaking on the 0.x line with no aliases kept. (#87)

tasks.title: The advertised surface can be trimmed (MCP surface is learnable, trimmable and honest)
tasks.description: ROADY_MCP_TOOLS selects which tool groups are registered, so a client does not pay prompt cost for a rate card or debt ledger the project does not have. A tool missing from the grouping must fail the build rather than silently vanish from every profile. (#87)

tasks.title: Error results survive strict schema validation (MCP surface is learnable, trimmable and honest)
tasks.description: A result with no structured payload must omit structuredContent rather than encode null, which matches no object schema and caused strict clients to reject the whole result including the text explaining the failure. roady asserts the wire format itself so a dependency change cannot reintroduce it invisibly. (#92)

tasks.title: Tool errors omit structuredContent on the wire (Trust: done means proven)
tasks.description: A failing tools/call (e.g. roady_task_transition on an unknown task) currently returns "structuredContent": null, because go.klarlabs.de/mcp applyStructuredResult writes the field unconditionally. Fix upstream and replace the marshal-only assertion with a test that drives a real tools/call. Done when: an end-to-end MCP test fails on null structuredContent and passes after the fix.

tasks.title: audit verify treats a removed or duplicated entry as alteration (Trust: done means proven)
tasks.description: A deleted middle entry is reported as 'referencing a removed parent' followed by 'nothing here is evidence of alteration' (cli/audit.go only checks KindHashMismatch). Done when: missing-parent and duplicate findings suppress the reassurance line and are summarised as evidence of alteration.

tasks.title: Detect truncation of the audit log tail (Trust: done means proven)
tasks.description: Removing the last N events verifies as intact. Anchor the head hash outside events.jsonl (e.g. state.json or a git ref) and compare on verify, or narrow the attestation wording. Done when: truncating the log fails audit verify.

tasks.title: setup claude-code registers MCP where Claude Code reads it (Trust: done means proven)
tasks.description: setup writes mcpServers into ~/.claude/settings.local.json and skips silently if the file exists. Register via project .mcp.json or `claude mcp add`, merge instead of skipping, and report what changed. Done when: after `roady setup claude-code` on a clean machine, roady tools are listed in a new Claude Code session.

tasks.title: Requirements and tasks carry an acceptance check (Trust: done means proven)
tasks.description: A check is a command, a named test, or a named manual check. `roady task verify` runs it and records the result, exit code and commit as evidence. Done when: a task with a check can be verified by running it, and the result is in the audit trail.

tasks.title: verified requires a linked commit and a passing check (Trust: done means proven)
tasks.description: The done -> verified transition is guarded: it needs at least one linked commit and a recorded passing check (or an explicit human override that is logged as such). Done when: an agent cannot move a task to verified without evidence, over CLI or MCP.

tasks.title: Drift re-runs the checks of verified tasks (Trust: done means proven)
tasks.description: `roady drift detect --checks` re-runs acceptance checks of verified tasks; a failing check is reported as regression drift with the task and commit. Done when: breaking the code behind a verified task makes drift report it.

check.run: go test ./internal/infrastructure/cli/ -run TestDriftChecksReportsARegression -count=1 && go test ./pkg/application/ -run TestRecheckVerified -count=1

tasks.title: A legitimate exit for impossible or conflicting work (Trust: done means proven)
tasks.description: Add a blocked reason 'spec-conflict' (and 'cannot-complete') the agent can choose instead of forcing done; it raises drift for a human to resolve. Research: offering an explicit abort cut test manipulation from 54% to 9% (ImpossibleBench). Done when: the transition exists in CLI and MCP and surfaces in status, report and drift.

check.run: go test ./pkg/application/ -run TestSpecConflictRaisesDriftUntilResolved -count=1 && go test ./internal/infrastructure/cli/ -run TestBlockWithASpecConflict -count=1 && go test ./internal/infrastructure/mcp/ -run TestBlockWithReasonOverMCP -count=1

tasks.title: One capture operation, idempotent upsert keyed by id (Capture: intent at whatever size it arrives)
tasks.description: `roady capture` (CLI, stdin JSON/YAML) and MCP `capture` accept goals, requirements and tasks with dependencies, in any quantity from one item to a full plan, and return what was created, changed and rejected. Replaces the spec_add -> plan_generate --ai -> plan_update -> approve round trip. Done when: an agent records a 10-task plan with dependencies in one call, and re-sending it is a no-op.

tasks.title: Ergonomic single-task commands (Capture: intent at whatever size it arrives)
tasks.description: `roady add`, `roady edit`, `roady split`, `roady move` as thin wrappers over capture, e.g. `roady add "Handle empty file" --req pdf-gen --after task-pdf-gen`. Done when: each command works without an editor and appears as one event in the audit log.

tasks.title: Approval is per change, not per plan (Capture: intent at whatever size it arrives)
tasks.description: Adding or splitting tasks within an existing requirement applies directly; adding or removing requirements or goals needs approval per policy.yaml. Today any regenerate resets the whole plan to pending. Done when: a single in-scope task add leaves the plan approved and its other tasks untouched.

tasks.title: Tasks without a requirement are allowed (Capture: intent at whatever size it arrives)
tasks.description: An ad-hoc task attaches to a goal or an inbox; drift reports it as 'unplanned work' (informational) rather than an orphan to prune. Done when: `roady add` with no --req succeeds and drift classifies it as unplanned.

check.run: go test ./internal/infrastructure/cli/ -run TestUnplannedTask -count=1 && go test ./pkg/domain/drift/ -run TestUnplannedIsNotAnOrphan -count=1

tasks.title: Edits that weaken done are guarded (Capture: intent at whatever size it arrives)
tasks.description: Title, notes, priority, dependencies and splits are freely editable. Tightening an acceptance check is free; loosening or removing it on an in-progress or verified task needs approval and reopens the task. The spec lock is not writable by the implementing agent. Done when: these rules are enforced in the domain layer for CLI and MCP alike, with tests.

tasks.title: Markdown import extracts requirements, not just headings (Capture: intent at whatever size it arrives)
tasks.description: parseMarkdownFile only turns '## ' headings into features and never creates requirements, so a normal PRD becomes 'Implement Overview'. Treat ###-sections as features and list items as requirements, skip overview-style sections, keep doc:line. Done when: the invoice-tool PRD from the evaluation imports as 3 features and 6 requirements.

tasks.title: Import plans from agent harness plan files (Capture: intent at whatever size it arrives)
tasks.description: Importers for Claude Code plan-mode files (~/.claude/plans or plansDirectory), Gemini CLI plans, Cursor .cursor/plans, Codex ExecPlans (PLANS.md) and Kiro .kiro/specs/*/tasks.md, mapping to capture. Done when: each format has a fixture test and `roady import <file>` detects the format.

tasks.title: setup installs Claude Code hooks (Capture: intent at whatever size it arrives)
tasks.description: Hooks: import the approved plan on ExitPlanMode; inject the current task brief on SessionStart and after compaction; block Write/Edit of ROADMAP*.md, TODO*.md and *plan*.md with a message pointing to capture (configurable allowlist). Done when: in a fresh project, approving a plan-mode plan lands it in roady with no manual step, and creating ROADMAP.md is redirected.

tasks.title: setup writes an instruction block and a planning skill (Capture: intent at whatever size it arrives)
tasks.description: Idempotent marked block in CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / GEMINI.md ('plans live in roady; never create ROADMAP.md/TODO.md/plan.md'), plus a roady planning skill for Claude Code. Done when: re-running setup updates the block in place and never duplicates it.

tasks.title: Default MCP surface of about six tools (Capture: intent at whatever size it arrives)
tasks.description: capture, next, update (claim/progress/block/complete), prove, status, query. The current ~70 tools (~16.5k tokens) stay behind ROADY_MCP_TOOLS=all. Reconciles the cli-mcp-parity constraint by capability rather than 1:1 tools: every CLI operation stays reachable. Done when: the default tools/list is under 3k tokens and the core loop needs no other tool.

tasks.title: Goals with horizons and milestones (Keep: continuity across sessions, compaction and parallel agents)
tasks.description: A Goal object with horizon now/next/later, optional milestone/release, and an idea state that needs no requirements yet. Features/requirements link to goals. Done when: roady's own ROADMAP.md content can be expressed without loss.

check.run: go test ./pkg/domain/spec/ -run Goal -count=1 && go test ./pkg/application/ -run 'Goal|Roadmap' -count=1 && go test ./internal/infrastructure/mcp/ -run TestGoalToolRecordsTheRoadmap -count=1 && go test ./internal/infrastructure/cli/ -run TestGoalCommands -count=1

tasks.title: Decision records linked to goals and requirements (Keep: continuity across sessions, compaction and parallel agents)
tasks.description: Lightweight decisions (context, choice, consequences, date) attached to goals or requirements, included in task briefs when relevant. Done when: `roady decide` records one and `roady next` shows decisions for the active task.

tasks.title: ROADMAP.md is generated from roady (Keep: continuity across sessions, compaction and parallel agents)
tasks.description: `roady render roadmap` writes ROADMAP.md with a generated header; drift flags hand edits to the rendered file. Done when: the rendered file round-trips and a manual edit is reported.

check.run: go test ./pkg/application/ -run 'Roadmap' -count=1 && go test ./internal/infrastructure/cli/ -run TestGoalRender -count=1 && go test ./internal/infrastructure/mcp/ -run TestGoalRenderOverMCP -count=1 && go run ./cmd/roady goal render --check

tasks.title: A compact task brief for re-injection (Keep: continuity across sessions, compaction and parallel agents)
tasks.description: `roady next --brief` (and MCP next) returns the active task, its acceptance check, dependencies, relevant decisions and source citation within a small token budget, for hooks at session start, after compaction and every N steps. Done when: the brief stays under 500 tokens for a typical task.

tasks.title: Task claims with an expiring lease (Keep: continuity across sessions, compaction and parallel agents)
tasks.description: Starting a task claims it for an actor/session with a lease that heartbeats and expires, so crashed agents do not hold tasks and two agents cannot take the same task. Done when: a concurrency test with two agents never double-claims, and an expired claim is released.

tasks.title: Execution state shared across worktrees and branches (Keep: continuity across sessions, compaction and parallel agents)
tasks.description: The plan stays in the repo for review; claims and progress live in one location all worktrees see (e.g. a git ref or the common git dir), so state is not forked per branch. Needs a decision record first. Done when: two worktrees see each other's claims and completions immediately.

tasks.title: Every plan edit is an appended event (Keep: continuity across sessions, compaction and parallel agents)
tasks.description: Splits, moves, edits and re-plans are recorded as events and the plan is derivable from them, rather than rewritten wholesale (avoids 'context collapse' from full rewrites). Done when: `roady timeline` shows a readable history of a task's splits and edits.

check.run: go test ./pkg/application/ -run TestTaskHistoryShowsSplitsAndEdits -count=1 && go test ./internal/infrastructure/cli/ -run TestTaskHistoryFromTheTerminal -count=1

tasks.title: Move peripheral features behind opt-in modules (Focus and proof of adoption)
tasks.description: Billing rates, cost reports, debt scoring, org views, the TUI and tracker syncers move behind opt-in modules or plugins; the default binary and docs present the core loop only. Done when: the README quickstart and default MCP surface reference none of them.

check.run: sed -n '1,/^## What Roady is, and is not/p' README.md | grep -qiE 'billing|cost report|debt scor|org view|dashboard|tracker sync|jira|linear' && exit 1; grep -hoE '"roady_(cost|debt|org|rate|team|sync|timeline|usage|forecast|messaging|plugin|report)[a-z_]*"' internal/infrastructure/mcp/*.go | grep -q . && exit 1; exit 0

tasks.title: Roady plans itself in roady (Focus and proof of adoption)
tasks.description: Migrate ROADMAP.md and docs/backlog.md into .roady and generate ROADMAP.md from it; the hand-written file is deleted. The 1.0 exit criterion. Done when: ROADMAP.md in this repo is generated and drift is clean with checks.

check.run: go run ./cmd/roady goal render --check && go run ./cmd/roady drift detect --checks && test ! -e docs/backlog.md

tasks.title: Local adoption metrics (Focus and proof of adoption)
tasks.description: `roady stats` reports, locally only: share of harness plans captured automatically, share of verified tasks with a passing check, and sessions that resumed on the right task without re-briefing. Done when: the three numbers are computed from the event log.

check.run: go test ./pkg/application/ -run TestComputeAdoptionStats -count=1 && go test ./internal/infrastructure/cli/ -run TestStatsCommand -count=1

tasks.title: setup for Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, Copilot and Kiro
tasks.description: Everything setup claude-code does, per agent where the agent supports it: MCP registration in the agent's project config, the instruction block (AGENTS.md / GEMINI.md / Kiro steering), the roady-planning skill in .agents/skills, and hooks (brief at session start, plan-file guard, plan import where a plan hook exists) with roady hook --agent formatting each agent's payload and output. Done when: setup <agent> writes a config each agent documents, re-running changes nothing, and each agent's hook payloads get correctly shaped answers.

tasks.title: Remove billing, team/org and integrations
tasks.description: Delete money & time (rates, tax, cost, budgets, time logging, usage, forecast), team & org (roster, roles, assignment, org rollups, workspace push/pull) and integrations (tracker sync plugins, messaging, webhooks, notify): CLI, MCP tools, services, domain packages, docs, tests. Task owner stays (claims need it). Done when: none of them is reachable from the CLI or MCP and the build and tests pass.

tasks.title: Cut the MCP server to the agent loop
tasks.description: MCP carries what an agent needs to work a plan: next, capture, plan import, transition, check, status, query, drift detect, semantic drift, dispatch. Governance (approve, reject, accept drift, lock), maintenance (init, prune, rebuild, validate, import/analyze spec, audit) and prompt builders stay on the CLI, so an agent cannot approve its own plan or accept its own drift. Done when: tools/list has about ten tools, the loop needs no other, and every removed operation is a CLI command.

tasks.title: MCP parity by CLI noun, with user approval for decisions
tasks.description: One MCP tool per CLI noun (init, next, status, query, capture, task, plan, spec, drift, audit, state, policy, git) with the CLI's verbs as actions, so every project operation is reachable over MCP. Decisions and destructive operations (plan approve/reject/prune, drift accept, spec lock/import/analyze, state rebuild) proceed only when the user confirms in their client (MCP elicitation); otherwise they are refused. Done when: every CLI verb has an MCP action, gated actions refuse without confirmation, and dead code is gone.
